title: Cairn module named queries (YAML)
$comment: A module's named, parameterised queries. This is how raw SQL leaves the web repository: a route calls a query by name with typed parameters, and the server binds them. Today the web layer splices a regex-checked vehicle id into SQL strings, and keeps a generated inventory of 88 of them; a named query with bound parameters removes that surface by construction rather than by care.

module.$comment: The owning module id. Must equal the manifest's.

name.$comment: Reached as POST /q/<module>/<name>. Unique within the module.

params.$comment: Every parameter must appear as $name in the SQL, and every $name in the SQL must be declared. The checker enforces both directions, so a query cannot silently ignore an argument or read an unbound one.

sql.$comment: One SELECT. Parameters are named placeholders ($vehicle_id), never interpolated text. A statement that is not a SELECT, or that holds a semicolon outside a string, is rejected: a query is a question, and nothing a module declares may write to the store.

age_threshold_ms.$comment: When the query relies on an ASOF join, the staleness bound it applies, repeated here so a reader can state it. An ASOF join always finds SOMETHING, so staleness has to be an explicit predicate and never a default -- the rule store/v1's views already follow.

type.$comment: vehicle_id and boot_id are 32 lowercase hex characters and are their own types because they are the two the store is partitioned by, and the two a caller is most likely to pass from a URL.
